parole.significato: Either of a pair of small drums of Cuban origin, played by beating with the hands.
parole.testo: From United States Spanish bongó, from a Bantu language; probably Ekele boungu.

parole.significato: Any of various grasses of the genus Hilaria (curly mesquite), of the southwestern US and northern Mexico.
parole.testo: From United States Spanish galleta, guieta, of unknown origin.
Borrowed from United States Spanish grocería, from English grocery.

parole.significato: Any of several species of fish of the genus Thunnus in the family Scombridae.
parole.testo: Borrowed from United States Spanish tuna, alteration of Spanish atún, from Arabic اَلتُّنّ (at-tunn, “tuna”), from Latin thunnus, itself from Ancient Greek θύννος (thúnnos). Possibly in the sense of "darter" from thynein "to dart along". Doublet of tonno.
